title: The Picard cohomology class commutes with arbitrary scheme pullback
statement: Let f:X→Y be any morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] and let L∈Pic(Y) [lem-sc-h1-gm-pic]. Under the canonical identification of Pic with H¹ of G_m, the cohomology pullback followed by the canonical G_m comparison sends the class of L to the class of f*L [def-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback], [def-pc-module-pullback]. No curve, field, finiteness or Noetherian hypothesis is needed.

source.place: Proof: Both defining components commute with base change, so the isomorphism does too; the Kummer description by the class of O(1).

proof.text: Represent the Picard class by its invertible module and use its torsor Isom(O,L) of trivializations. Pull a trivialization over an etale Y-scheme V back along V×_Y X→V, and use f*O_Y≅O_X. The resulting maps to the trivialization torsor of f*L are natural in V and equivariant for the pullback of units.

The pullback-and-coefficient-change naturality of torsor H¹ classes identifies the image of the first torsor class with the second. Rewriting both classes using Pic.toCohomologicalPicardGroup gives the equality. This is the complete existing proof of Scheme.gmCohomologyMap_toCohomologicalPicardGroup for arbitrary schemes.

theorem gmCohomologyMap_toCohomologicalPicardGroup (L : Y.Pic) :
    gmCohomologyMap g 1 (Pic.toCohomologicalPicardGroup Y L) =
      Pic.toCohomologicalPicardGroup X (Pic.map g L)
